claims.claim: Ford introduced the first moving automobile assembly line on October 7, 1913, at the Highland Park plant.
claims.episode_span: Then a moving line appeared on the floor at Highland Park
claims.supporting_quote: This month marks the official celebration of the world’s first moving assembly line. On Oct. 7, 1913, 140 assemblers stationed along a 150-foot chassis line at a Ford Motor Co. plant just north of Detroit stood in place as the work came to them.

claims.claim: Engine assembly time fell from 594 minutes to 226 minutes after the moving line was introduced.
claims.episode_span: The work took roughly 594 minutes for a single engine. Then a moving line appeared on the floor at Highland Park, and the same engine reached completion in 226 minutes.
claims.supporting_quote: By using a moving line, engine assembly time was slashed from 594 minutes to 226 minutes.

claims.claim: Model T runabout price started at $825 in 1909 and reached a low of $260 by 1925.
claims.episode_span: The 1909 Model T runabout sold for $825
claims.supporting_quote: A Model T runabout cost $825 for the 1909 model year and $440 in 1914, and it reached its low of $260 in 1925.
